line/arc: Take a two pixel image, x zero, as a point in the plane, and its noise epsilon as another. As alpha bar falls, the diffusion blend travels from one to the other along a curve.
line/line: Flow matching takes the straight line instead. x t is one minus t, times x zero, plus t times epsilon, with t running from zero, the image, to one, pure noise.
line/point: Say x zero is one and zero, and epsilon is minus one and two. At t of a quarter, take three quarters of x zero plus a quarter of epsilon: a half, and a half.
line/v: Along the line, the point moves at a steady velocity, v: epsilon minus x zero, here minus two and two, for each unit of t. It is the same at every t.
train/net: Train the network as before, with a new target. It sees x t and t, and guesses the velocity: v hat, the hat marking a guess of v.
train/loss: The loss is the squared error against epsilon minus x zero, averaged. A guess of minus one and a half, and two, misses by a half and by zero: the loss is a quarter over two, zero point one two five.
sample/start: To make an image, start at t equals one, with pure noise, and walk back to zero.
sample/euler: Each Euler step asks the network for v hat at the current point, and moves against it: the new x t is the old one minus delta t times v hat, where delta t is the step's size in t. Then t drops by delta t.
sample/ex: Start from minus one and two, with delta t of a half. If the guess is minus two and two, the step adds one and takes away one: the point lands on zero and one, at t of a half.
sample/exact: A second step lands on one and zero: the image. On a straight line the velocity never changes, so even one long step would land exactly.
sample/bend: But the network never sees which image a noise came from, so its velocity is an average over every line through the point, and its paths bend a little. A few steps follow them well.
